title: Nothing ties dispatcherIndex's primeToken to the contract's funding assets, and the removed deploy-time guard was not replaced by an operator-facing one
description: The §4.1 exclusion key and the payment asset are both derived live from `dispatcher.primeToken()`. Repointing the dispatcher — here via `setDispatcherIndex`, or in the SIBLING repo via `NFTMinterV2.replaceDispatcher` — silently reclassifies existing balances. story-022 removed the deploy-time 'nudge token == payment token' assertion and replaced it with a per-call revert that warns the CALLER, never the OPERATOR.
impact: Two consequences of one routine action. (1) AVAILABILITY: if the pinned dispatcher's primeToken() equals the token it donates to batchMinter, the nudge becomes STRUCTURALLY DEAD — every legitimate claim reverts BatchMint__RewardTokenIsPaymentToken. (2) VALUE: the accumulated pot simultaneously becomes fully sweepable by any count==1 caller (CLASS-002). One operator action arms both.
attackPath: 1. story-022 removed the deploy-time 'nudge token == payment token' assertion and replaced it with a per-call revert that warns the CALLER, never the OPERATOR.
2. An operator repoints the dispatcher — via setDispatcherIndex here, or via NFTMinterV2.replaceDispatcher in the SIBLING repo, where nothing surfaces this coupling.
3. The §4.1 exclusion key and the payment asset are both derived live from dispatcher.primeToken(), so existing balances are silently reclassified.
4. The nudge is now structurally dead and the pot is sweepable.

5. Not hypothetical: yield-claim-nft/src/dispatchers/PromotionUniV2_Eth.sol has primeToken()==USDC (:189) AND donates USDC to batchMinter (:340); NudgeRatchet.sol likewise forwards USDC. Only the currently-pinned BalancerPoolerV2 (USDS prime, USDC donation) is safe.
likelihood: medium — the script's own NatSpec flags DISPATCHER_INDEX = 4 as 'ASSUMED … the operator MUST confirm', i.e. a repoint is an EXPECTED operation, and two of the three real dispatchers in the sibling repo are unsafe.
assumptions: The operator repoints to a dispatcher whose primeToken equals its donated asset. Two of three live candidates satisfy this.
externalRequirements: A cross-repo action in yield-claim-nft, performed by an operator who has no signal from this contract that it matters.
justification: C4 Medium as a Law-3 OPERATIONAL HAZARD, on the AVAILABILITY ground. Repointing the dispatcher is a documented, EXPECTED maintenance action — the deploy script's own NatSpec flags DISPATCHER_INDEX = 4 as 'ASSUMED … the operator MUST confirm' — and it is performed in a DIFFERENT REPOSITORY (yield-claim-nft, NFTMinterV2.replaceDispatcher) with no signal there that it matters. When the pinned dispatcher's primeToken() equals the token it donates, the nudge mechanism ceases to function for its legitimate users outright: every qualifying claim reverts BatchMint__RewardTokenIsPaymentToken. TWO OF THE THREE real dispatchers in the sibling repo satisfy the unsafe condition today (PromotionUniV2_Eth primeToken()==USDC at :189 and donates USDC at :340; NudgeRatchet likewise forwards USDC; only the currently-pinned BalancerPoolerV2 is safe). That is an availability impact on a protocol function arising from an expected operation, with a real external requirement — the literal C4 Medium shape. Law 3 is satisfied: no malicious-owner vector is asserted, and the surprise test is answered yes.
recommendation: Restore an operator-facing deploy/setter assertion that resolves configs(DISPATCHER_INDEX).dispatcher.primeToken() and compares it against the intended reward asset. The on-chain per-call check reverts the caller; it does not warn the operator.
